body.statement:
For every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\) and \(S\in\mathcal A\), \(
u_S^2(\vartheta)=0\) if and only if \(b_S(\vartheta)=0\), equivalently \(\mu_0=\mu_1\), \(\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}c_{0,S}=\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}c_{1,S}\), and \(r_0(S)=r_1(S)\). Hence every equality parameter is excluded from \(\Theta_+(
u_*)\) for every fixed \(
u_*>0\).
body.justification: The equivalence isolates the quadratic equality boundary and makes the domains of ordinary Wald and projection inference disjoint where first-order studentization fails.
body.gap: Lin et al. identify equality as a degeneracy point for a fixed quadratic transport target; this proposition records the exact Gaussian selected-endpoint criterion needed to route inference, without claiming a new generic selection principle.
body.consumer: Analysts can determine from the moment parameter whether to use separated Wald inference or the whole-image projection interval.
